OSPS-AC-01.01_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide: GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation, covering repository write access and private vulnerability reports alike.
OSPS-AC-02.01_justification: Collaborator permissions are assigned explicitly, never inherited by default. The repository baseline script sets the default repository permission to the lowest privilege and review routing goes through CODEOWNERS to the `owners` team; the settings are code, applied and drift-checked by settings/repo-baseline.sh. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
OSPS-AC-03.01_justification: An organisation-level ruleset blocks direct pushes to main: every change must arrive as a pull request and pass required status checks. The rules and their rationale are recorded in docs/rulesets.md and the Monday audit re-checks them for drift. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
OSPS-AC-03.02_justification: The organisation ruleset restricts branch deletion on the primary branch, so deleting main is refused rather than confirmed away. Recorded in docs/rulesets.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
OSPS-AC-04.01_justification: Least privilege is the default and the explicit setting: the repository baseline sets the workflow token to read-only permissions, and every workflow declares its own minimal `permissions:` block on top of that. A job that specifies nothing therefore gets read, not write. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
OSPS-AC-04.02_justification: Every workflow declares an explicit `permissions:` block scoped to what that job actually needs, on top of a read-only default set by the repository baseline. The strongest case is enforced by a lint: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may hold `id-token: write`, and lint:capability-boundary fails the build if one ever does.
OSPS-BR-01.01_justification: Untrusted workflow metadata is validated before use: the shared workflows accept inputs against allowlists (the artifact `classes:` set, the pinned publish stub shape checked by lint:release-stub), and zizmor fails the gate on template-injection patterns where untrusted context would reach a shell.
OSPS-BR-01.03_justification: This repository declares no reusable workflow, so it runs no caller-supplied code; its workflows are entry points whose privileged steps are delegated to the organisation's SHA-pinned shared workflows, and the boundary rule that forbids `id-token: write` in any workflow that runs caller code is enforced there by lint:capability-boundary — with this repository as the foreign caller that proves it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CLAUDE.md
OSPS-BR-01.04_justification: Collaborator-supplied input is validated rather than trusted: workflow inputs are checked against allowlists (the artifact `classes:` set, the release-stub shape), and zizmor fails the gate on any pattern that would interpolate untrusted context into a shell.
OSPS-BR-02.01_justification: Every release is a unique semantic version, derived from conventional commits by git-cliff and tagged v<major>.<minor>.<patch> by the release App; the tag ruleset makes tags immutable, so a version identifier is never reused.
OSPS-BR-02.02_justification: Verified on the published release: every asset is named for the release identifier (release-lab-0.24.4-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz, lab_pg-0.24.4-pg18-linux-amd64.tar.gz, release-lab-0.24.4.spdx.json) and each is additionally bound by cryptographic digest in checksums.txt and in the attestations. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/releases/tag/v0.24.4
OSPS-BR-03.01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS: the repository, releases, documentation and issue tracker are all served by GitHub over TLS, and no plaintext URI appears in the tree.
OSPS-BR-03.02_justification: Distribution is over HTTPS and authenticated beyond transport: releases carry Sigstore evidence bundles and GitHub artifact attestations, and every consumed tool is pinned with per-platform checksums in mise.lock, so a substituted artifact fails verification rather than merely a certificate check.
OSPS-BR-04.01_justification: CHANGELOG.md is generated by git-cliff from conventional commits and the same descriptive log is attached to each GitHub release, so every functional and security modification is recorded per version. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
OSPS-BR-05.01_justification: Dependency ingestion is standardised and locked: cargo with a committed Cargo.lock for crates, mise with a lockfile carrying per-platform checksums for tools, base images by digest, and cargo-deny restricting sources to a single registry with unknown-registry and unknown-git denied.
OSPS-BR-06.01_justification: Each release carries Sigstore evidence bundles and GitHub artifact attestations covering every published asset by cryptographic digest — nine bundles on v0.24.4 — and the governance repository's runbook documents how a consumer verifies them. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md#verifying-as-a-consumer-would
OSPS-BR-07.01_justification: Secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, so an unencrypted credential is blocked at push time; trivy's secret rules also run in the gate. The architecture removes most of the risk at source: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, so there are few long-lived secrets to leak.
OSPS-BR-07.02_justification: docs/continuity.md is the secrets policy in operational form: an asset table naming every credential the project uses, where it is stored, who can reach it, and how it is rotated or recreated — including the one standing token, whose expiry is designed to fail loudly rather than silently under-claim. The policy is short because the architecture removes most secrets: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, and no signing key exists to store. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
OSPS-DO-01.01_justification: README.md documents what this repository is, what it exercises and how it is run; the machinery it calls is documented in the governance repository's docs/runbook.md and docs/release.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
OSPS-DO-02.01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the repository's issue forms document how to report a defect, and SECURITY.md documents the separate private path for vulnerabilities. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
OSPS-DO-03.01_justification: The governance repository's runbook has a section written from the consumer's position — 'Verifying as a consumer would' — giving the commands to check a release's attestations and evidence bundle against the published digests. Every release of this repository is verified that way before the machinery is relied on elsewhere. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md#verifying-as-a-consumer-would
OSPS-DO-03.02_justification: The same documentation covers authorship identity, which in a keyless design is the workflow identity: verification checks the signer's workflow ref in the certificate rather than a personal key, and the release tooling exposes an explicit signer-workflow flag so a consumer can assert which identity must have signed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
OSPS-DO-04.01_justification: SECURITY.md states the support scope explicitly: only the latest release of each project receives security updates, fixes ship by rolling forward rather than backporting, and there are no long-term support branches. This repository is additionally documented as a lab whose versions are spent freely. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-DO-05.01_justification: SECURITY.md states the end-of-life rule in the same section: a release is supported exactly until the next release exists, at which point it is end-of-life for security purposes. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-DO-06.01_justification: Documented in two places and deliberately so: docs/tooling-verdicts.md records how a dependency is selected — the priors a tool must meet to enter the belt, and the verdicts on tools considered and declined — and docs/dependency-track.md records how dependencies are obtained, pinned, monitored and triaged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/tooling-verdicts.md
OSPS-DO-07.01_justification: README.md gives the whole sequence: `mise trust && mise install` brings every required tool at its pinned version from the lockfile, and `mise run ci` then runs exactly what CI runs. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
OSPS-GV-01.01_justification: docs/continuity.md carries an asset table naming who holds each sensitive resource — organisation ownership, the tag-mint App key, registry accounts, the one standing token — and what happens to each if that person is unavailable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
OSPS-GV-01.02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and the responsibilities of each, and it is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file so it applies to every repository that does not carry its own. Who holds the maintainer role is explicit: the @monumental-archive/owners team, which CODEOWNERS routes every review to. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
OSPS-GV-02.01_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests are open for public discussion of proposed changes and usage obstacles; both are searchable and individually addressable by URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/issues
OSPS-GV-03.01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: open an issue first for anything large, pull requests for small self-contained fixes, Conventional Commits, DCO sign-off, a green `mise run ci`, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
OSPS-GV-03.02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md includes a 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: pull request only, a green `mise run ci`, Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects under 72 columns, DCO sign-off, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
OSPS-GV-04.01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md's 'Escalation and permissions' section states the policy: a collaborator is reviewed before being granted any escalated permission — who they are, why the access is needed, and the smallest sufficient grant — and the grant is recorded in the settings-as-code baseline so drift is auditable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
OSPS-LE-01.01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1 sign-off asserting legal authorisation. The commit-msg hook catches a missing trailer locally and lint:dco fails the gate, with no exemption list — automation signs off too.
OSPS-LE-02.01_justification: Every file in this repository is 0BSD, an OSI-approved and FSF-free licence; the crate metadata additionally declares `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, both of which are OSI-approved and FSF-free as well. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/LICENSE
OSPS-LE-02.02_justification: The released assets carry a FLOSS licence, and the licensing is two grants rather than one — deliberately, with one copyright holder, so both hold at once. Every file in the repository is 0BSD (REUSE.toml, the whole tree), while the package metadata built from Cargo.toml declares `MIT OR Apache-2.0`: the published @monumental-archive/lab-wasm@0.24.4 carries "license": "MIT OR Apache-2.0" on npm, and LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE sit beside LICENSE in the tree. The compound expression is a deliberate fixture input — it is how the wasm-pack to package.json to npm path gets exercised — and it grants more restrictively than the source does, never less. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/REUSE.toml
OSPS-LE-03.01_justification: LICENSE at the repository root with the full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt, the REUSE-standard location, alongside LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE for the licences the crate metadata declares. `reuse lint` passes and lint:reuse enforces it in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/LICENSE
OSPS-LE-03.02_justification: Released assets are built from this repository, which carries LICENSE, LICENSES/0BSD.txt, LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE at its root, and the packages themselves carry their SPDX expression in their metadata — verified on the published npm package for v0.24.4. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/LICENSE
OSPS-QA-01.01_justification: Publicly readable at a static URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab
OSPS-QA-01.02_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, for every revision, and the history is public. Each revision additionally carries a signed source-provenance attestation emitted by this repository's own reserved identity, so the record is independently verifiable.
OSPS-QA-02.01_justification: Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock enumerate every crate dependency with an exact resolved version; mise.toml and mise.lock do the same for tools with per-platform checksums. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/Cargo.lock
OSPS-QA-02.02_justification: Every release ships an SPDX software bill of materials as a release asset — verified on v0.24.4: release-lab-0.24.4.spdx.json and release-lab-0.24.4-image.spdx.json, alongside the binaries, the extension packages, checksums.txt, the OpenVEX document and the evidence bundles. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/releases/tag/v0.24.4
OSPS-QA-03.01_justification: gate.yml is a required status check on main under an organisation ruleset: direct pushes are blocked entirely and a pull request cannot merge red, so no commit reaches the default branch without the full gate — the lint belt, `cargo test --workspace --locked` and the coverage ratchet — having passed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
OSPS-QA-04.01_justification: The project is this single repository and its scope is documented in README.md: which artefact classes it exercises for real, which is rehearsed dry, and what each fixture crate is for. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
OSPS-QA-04.02_justification: A release of this project comprises this single source repository; there are no subprojects releasing alongside it.
OSPS-QA-05.01_justification: No generated executable artifacts are committed. The only tracked non-source files are libFuzzer corpus inputs under fuzz/corpus — small opaque byte strings that are test data, not code, and regenerable by running the fuzzer; build outputs live in target/, which is ignored.
OSPS-QA-05.02_justification: No unreviewable binary artifacts are committed: every tracked file is either text or a libFuzzer corpus input, and a corpus input is inspectable test data whose provenance is the fuzzer itself.
OSPS-QA-06.01_justification: gate.yml runs the full automated suite — the shared lint belt, `cargo test --workspace --locked` and the coverage ratchet — on every pull request before it can be accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
OSPS-QA-06.02_justification: Documented in both places a reader would look: README.md states that `mise run ci` locally is exactly what CI runs, and CONTRIBUTING.md makes a green gate a requirement for every change.
OSPS-QA-06.03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' item 3, states the policy in the contributor-facing documentation: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it, and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
OSPS-QA-07.01_justification: With a single maintainer there is no non-author human approval available, so this is not enforced. It is the headcount wall this project records rather than works around: the same boundary as Gold's two_person_review and SLSA Source L4, tracked as an open issue rather than quietly claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
OSPS-SA-01.01_justification: The pipeline this repository runs is specified actor by actor and action by action in the governance repository's docs/release.md, and this repository's README maps each of its own caller stubs — gate, release, publish, continuous, exercise-sign, source-attest, audit, audit-repro, scorecard — to what that stub proves. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
OSPS-SA-02.01_justification: The external interfaces are the caller stubs' inputs and the published packages. Each stub and its inputs are documented in README.md here and specified in the governance repository's docs/runbook.md; the published artefacts are the crate, the npm package, the images and the per-major extension packages, each named and described per release. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
OSPS-SA-03.01_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are written security assessments of this system: they walk the controls, name the most likely and impactful failure modes (untrusted caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, supply-chain substitution through unpinned dependencies, silent settings drift), and record which are mitigated and which are accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
OSPS-SA-03.02_justification: docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md carry the threat model and attack-surface analysis: the critical paths are named (caller code reaching a privileged signing identity, unpinned supply-chain substitution, silent settings drift, forged signer identities in the transparency log), each with the control that protects it and the residual risk accepted. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
OSPS-VM-01.01_justification: SECURITY.md is the coordinated disclosure policy and it states the timeframe: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, and what the reporter can expect afterwards. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-VM-02.01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact and the reporting channel: private vulnerability reporting through the repository's Security tab, with a 14-day acknowledgement commitment. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-VM-03.01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, delivering the report directly to the security contact without public exposure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-VM-04.01_justification: Vulnerability data for this repository is published rather than held privately: a resolved report would be published as a GitHub Security Advisory here, and dependency findings already ship publicly with every release as an OpenVEX document (release-lab-0.24.4.vex.openvex.json) recording each decision against the release's SBOM. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/releases/tag/v0.24.4
OSPS-VM-04.02_justification: The release path emits OpenVEX documents keyed by package@version recording non-exploitability decisions, shipped as a release asset (release-lab-0.24.4.vex.openvex.json) — and it is enforced, not optional: publishing is refused while an advisory in the SBOM is undecided, which blocked v0.19.1 until RUSTSEC-2021-0127 was decided. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/releases/tag/v0.24.4
OSPS-VM-05.01_justification: docs/dependency-track.md defines the thresholds: cargo-deny bans and licence rules are deterministic and fail the gate, sources are restricted to a single registry with unknown-registry and unknown-git denied, and every advisory must exit through an explicit decision rather than being left open. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
OSPS-VM-05.02_justification: The policy is enforced at the release boundary, not merely stated: the release path refuses to publish with an undecided advisory in its SBOM. It has already blocked a real release in the lab rather than being theoretical. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
OSPS-VM-05.03_justification: Automatically, on every change: cargo-deny runs deterministically in the gate over the lockfile and the committed deny.toml, dependency-review runs on every pull request, and Renovate and Dependabot raise updates as advisories land. The policy those checks enforce is written in docs/dependency-track.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
OSPS-VM-06.01_justification: SECURITY.md's 'Static analysis policy' states the remediation threshold and it is zero: any static-analysis finding fails the gate, a red gate cannot merge, and there is therefore no state in which a finding is outstanding on the default branch. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-VM-06.02_justification: Every change is automatically evaluated and blocked on violation: CodeQL is enforced organisation-wide, and cargo-deny, osv-scanner, shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor and trivy run in the gate, which is a required status check.
access_continuity_justification: docs/continuity.md is exactly this document: assets and their recovery paths, a break-glass procedure for the tag-minting App, a succession plan, and an explicit list of deliberate single points of failure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project has no bespoke website: documentation is plain Markdown rendered by GitHub, which is keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly, and the content is text with descriptive link text rather than images carrying meaning.
assurance_case_justification: docs/release.md and docs/slsa-reference.md in the governance repository are the written assurance case for this pipeline, and the assessments walk each claim against its evidence. What this repository adds is the execution: the claims are demonstrated here at full width before they are relied on anywhere. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: gate.yml runs on every push and every pull request to main and reports as a required status check; beyond it, the release path itself runs end to end on every version — four artefact classes, five Postgres majors, real registries. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
build_common_tools_justification: cargo and rustc, at a version pinned in mise.toml (with wasm-pack, cargo-pgrx and cargo-auditable for the class-specific builds) — the standard build tooling of the language.
build_floss_tools_justification: The entire toolchain is FLOSS: rustc, cargo, wasm-pack, cargo-pgrx, cargo-auditable, cargo-fuzz and mise itself.
build_justification: The software is Rust: `cargo build --workspace` builds it from source, and the release path builds the same tree into binaries, an OCI image, a wasm npm package and per-Postgres-major extension packages. The toolchain is pinned in mise.toml and installed by `mise install`. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/mise.toml
build_non_recursive_justification: No recursive build system is used: cargo builds the workspace as a single graph.
build_preserve_debug_justification: `cargo build` without `--release` produces debugging information by default, and the release profile's debug setting is a one-line change in Cargo.toml.
build_repeatable_justification: Proven on every release, not asserted: each artefact class is built twice independently in the publish workflow and the repro gate compares the two outputs bit for bit before anything is signed or attached, across rust-binary, oci-image, wasm-npm and pgrx-extension for every supported Postgres major. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/release.md
build_reproducible_justification: Reproducible and independently re-verified: beyond the per-release repro gate, audit-repro.yml rebuilds the latest published release from cold on a weekly schedule and compares the result against the published digests. This repository is where that check first caught real image nondeterminism. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/.github/workflows/audit-repro.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: Cargo honours the language's standard build variables (RUSTFLAGS, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, and CC/AR for build scripts); no wrapper overrides them.
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1 — a single maintainer. Recorded plainly in docs/slsa-reference.md as headcount-blocked, with docs/continuity.md carrying the succession and break-glass paths that exist precisely because of it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
code_of_conduct_justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md at the repository root, in the standard location, and served as the organisation default to every repository in the org. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: GOVERNANCE.md's 'Code review' section states how review is conducted, what a reviewer checks (that the change does what it says, that its claim is one its checks enforce, that it weakens no documented control, that documentation moved with behaviour), what makes a change acceptable, and that the mechanical floor is the gate's job rather than the reviewer's. It also records plainly that with one maintainer there is no second human reviewer. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Automatically, in the gate: the belt's linters run in `mise run ci` on every pull request and `fix:*` siblings apply the machine-fixable subset. Style is never a review comment here.
coding_standards_justification: The gate is the coding standard in executable form, and it is specific per language: rustfmt's default style for Rust with clippy available locally, shellcheck for shell with bash pinned, actionlint and zizmor for workflow YAML, taplo for TOML, rumdl for Markdown, typos for spelling and committed for commit shape. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, served to this repository as the organisation default, documents the process: fork/branch, conventional imperative commit subjects under 72 columns enforced by committed, DCO sign-off, `mise run ci` green locally, pull request, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Requirements for acceptable contributions': every change arrives by pull request, must pass `mise run ci` (the coding standard in executable form), uses Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects, and is squash-merged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: There is one significant contributor, so there cannot be two unassociated ones. Headcount, not policy: contributions are welcomed under CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
copyright_per_file_justification: Every file carries a copyright statement, attached through REUSE.toml rather than an inline header — the REUSE specification's supported mechanism. `reuse lint` reports 180 of 180 files with copyright information, and lint:reuse enforces it in the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/REUSE.toml
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The software implements no cryptography and selects no algorithms; where cryptography is used it is Sigstore's and GitHub's.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptographic operations are delegated to software built for the purpose — Sigstore/cosign, GitHub's attestation tooling and git — never reimplemented here.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Certificate verification is never disabled: there is no `--insecure`, `-k`, or `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY` anywhere in the tracked tree, so every HTTPS call made by the project verifies by default.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The software stores no authentication credentials or private keys. Secrets live in GitHub environment and organisation secrets, never in files in the repository, and release signing uses ephemeral keys.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography relied on is FLOSS: Sigstore, cosign and git.
crypto_keylength_justification: The software selects no keylengths. Release signing uses ephemeral Sigstore keys with Fulcio-issued certificates, and transport keys belong to GitHub and the registries.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software stores no passwords and authenticates no external users.
crypto_pfs_justification: The fixture crates implement no key agreement protocol; they are a library, a CLI, a wasm package and a Postgres extension, none of them a network service.
crypto_published_justification: The fixture crates implement no cryptography of their own. Where the release path relies on cryptography it uses published, expert-reviewed mechanisms: Sigstore (Fulcio certificates, Rekor transparency log), GitHub artifact attestations, npm provenance and SHA-256 digests.
crypto_random_justification: The software generates no cryptographic keys or nonces; release signing keys are generated by Sigstore.
crypto_tls12_justification: The software does not implement or configure TLS; it invokes tools (cargo, git, gh, curl) whose TLS versions are theirs.
crypto_used_network_justification: All network communication is HTTPS — GitHub APIs, tool downloads, registry publishing, transparency-log submission. No insecure protocol appears anywhere in the tree, and certificate verification is never disabled.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The software implements no TLS client of its own and sends no HTTP headers carrying private information.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Integrity everywhere is SHA-256 and signing is Sigstore's ECDSA P-256. No MD5 or SHA-1 is relied on as a security mechanism.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is depended on for security: artifact integrity is SHA-256 (checksums.txt, image digests, attestation subjects, mise.lock) and signing is Sigstore's ECDSA P-256.
dco_justification: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1. Every commit must carry Signed-off-by; the commit-msg hook catches it locally and lint:dco enforces it in the gate, with no exemption list — the release commit and Renovate sign off too. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
delivery_mitm_justification: Everything is delivered over HTTPS by GitHub, GHCR and npm. Beyond transport, every dependency is pinned: Cargo.lock for crates, mise.lock with per-platform checksums for tools, full commit SHAs for every `uses:`, and image bases by digest.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Checksums are not fetched over http at use time: they travel with the source in Cargo.lock and mise.lock, and every published release carries Sigstore evidence bundles and GitHub artifact attestations that a consumer can verify against the digest.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Continuously: cargo-deny and osv-scanner run in the gate over the lockfile, dependency-review runs on every pull request, Renovate and Dependabot open updates as advisories land, and the release path emits VEX decisions keyed by package@version for anything undecided. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
description_good_justification: The README states what this is in its first lines: the organisation's release lab, where risky release machinery is proven against real GitHub APIs, real credentials, real rulesets and real registries before any production repository runs it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests: searchable, individually addressable by URL, open to new participants, and archived publicly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/issues
documentation_achievements_justification: The README carries a derived badge block linking every achievement — OpenSSF Scorecard, the three SLSA track levels, REUSE compliance, the archived DOI, the published packages and this badge. The block is rendered from the repository's own facts by `mise run fix:badges` and a lint fails the build when it drifts. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: README.md documents the architecture in two tables — each fixture crate and the artefact class it feeds, each caller stub and what it proves — and the machinery those stubs call is specified in the governance repository's docs/release.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
documentation_basics_justification: README.md documents what the repository is for, what each fixture crate feeds, what each caller stub proves, and what proving here has already caught; the machinery it exercises is specified in the governance repository's docs/release.md and docs/runbook.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
documentation_current_justification: Documentation is updated in the same pull request as the change it describes, the README's badge block is derived from the tree and lint-checked, and the scheduled audit re-checks link liveness so stale documentation surfaces on a cadence.
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface of this repository is its caller stubs and their inputs, documented per stub in README.md and specified in full in the governance repository's docs/runbook.md and docs/release.md; the fixture crates' own surface is small and carries rustdoc comments. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/runbook.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md opens with what this repository is and how it is used, and the developer path is two commands: `mise trust && mise install`, then `mise run ci`. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: The governance repository's docs/direction.md is the roadmap, including what will deliberately not be done; this repository's README states its own scope precisely — which classes are rehearsed for real, which is rehearsed dry (rust-crate, never uploaded to crates.io), and why. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/direction.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md states what users may expect (private reporting, 14-day acknowledgement, supported versions, the zero remediation threshold for static findings), and docs/slsa-reference.md states the security properties claimed and the ones deliberately not claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz and test builds are debug builds: `debug_assertions` and integer overflow checks are on, so assertion failures and overflows abort rather than pass silently.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No fuzzing finding is outstanding. A crash or panic fails audit:fuzz with the reproducer path in the log, and interesting inputs are committed to the in-tree corpus so the case stays covered.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Fuzzing runs, and it satisfies this criterion's own definition of a tool that varies its inputs: cargo-fuzz drives libFuzzer against the parse_marker target with a committed in-tree corpus. The deterministic half (lint:fuzz-build) is in the gate on every pull request so a target that stops compiling fails the build; the time-bound half (audit:fuzz) runs the targets on the scheduled audit and fails with a reproducer path on any crash or panic. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/tree/main/fuzz
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: No memory-unsafe language is used: the crates are safe Rust with no `unsafe` blocks in the tracked sources, which is why the fuzz targets build with `--sanitizer none` on the pinned stable toolchain — in safe Rust the failure class libFuzzer surfaces is the panic, not the buffer overwrite.
english_justification: All documentation, code comments, issues and commit messages are in English.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are filed as issues, triaged and either closed with a linked pull request or closed with the reason recorded; the two closed issues here were resolved that way and none is left unanswered.
external_dependencies_justification: Machine-readable and pinned throughout: Cargo.toml plus a committed Cargo.lock for crate dependencies, mise.toml plus mise.lock with per-platform checksums for tools, deny.toml for the licence and source policy, and renovate.json driving automated updates. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/Cargo.toml
floss_license_justification: Every file in the repository is released under 0BSD, a FLOSS licence, declared for the whole tree by REUSE.toml and enforced in the gate by lint:licence and lint:reuse. The workspace crates additionally declare `MIT OR Apache-2.0` in Cargo.toml: that is deliberate and both grants hold at once, there being one copyright holder — the compound expression is a fixture input that exercises the wasm-pack -> package.json -> npm path and keeps the crates inside the shared cargo-deny allowlist. Both licences are FLOSS. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: 0BSD (BSD Zero Clause License) is OSI-approved, as are MIT and Apache-2.0, the licences the crate metadata declares. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/LICENSE
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the decision model explicitly rather than aspirationally: one maintainer deciding in the open, significant decisions made in writing and in public before they are implemented (the docs-first standup, recorded as issues and pull requests), declined paths recorded with reasons so they are re-litigated against the record, and a written succession plan. It is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file, so it governs every repository that does not carry its own. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: The project site is the GitHub repository itself, which is served with hardening headers: strict-transport-security with a one-year max-age and includeSubdomains, content-security-policy with default-src 'none', x-frame-options: deny, and x-content-type-options: nosniff. There is no separate project or download site to harden.
hardening_justification: Least-privilege permissions on every workflow; every `uses:` pinned to a full commit SHA; the toolchain pinned with per-platform checksums in mise.lock and Cargo dependencies locked; keyless publishing with no standing credentials; secret scanning with push protection enforced organisation-wide; releases immutable once published.
implement_secure_design_justification: Implemented, not merely known: every workflow in this repository declares a minimal explicit `permissions:` block, the logic it calls is pinned to a full commit SHA of the governance repository, publishing is keyless via OIDC trusted publishing with no standing credentials, and each release is signed and attested through the organisation's separate signer identity, which never sees the bytes it signs.
input_validation_justification: The fixture crates validate their inputs and are fuzzed for it: parse_marker is a libFuzzer target with a committed corpus, run under audit:fuzz and built in the gate by lint:fuzz-build. The workflow surface validates inputs against allowlists in the shared workflows this repository calls (the artifact `classes:` set, the publish stub shape checked by lint:release-stub).
installation_common_justification: Every published class installs by the standard mechanism of its ecosystem: `cargo install` or the release tarball for the binary, `npm install @monumental-archive/lab-wasm` for the wasm package, `docker pull ghcr.io/monumental-archive/release-lab` for the image, and the per-major extension packages for Postgres. Nothing requires a bespoke installer.
installation_development_quick_justifica: `mise trust && mise install` installs the pinned Rust toolchain and every tool the gate uses from the lockfile; `mise run ci` then runs exactly what CI runs. That is the whole developer setup. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: The build honours the standard Rust conventions — CARGO_TARGET_DIR, RUSTFLAGS, CARGO_INSTALL_ROOT — and the release tarballs are relocatable, so an installer chooses its own prefix.
interact_justification: GitHub serves this repository the organisation's community health files from monumental-archive/.github — CONTRIBUTING.md (how to contribute), SUPPORT.md (how to get help), CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, SECURITY.md (how to report a vulnerability), the issue forms and the pull-request template — and the README links the governance repository directly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
interfaces_current_justification: Dependencies are held current by automated updates rather than allowed to drift, and actionlint fails the gate on deprecated GitHub Actions features, so obsolescence surfaces as a red build.
internationalization_justification: The software produced is shell tasks, workflows and configuration; it emits maintainer-facing diagnostics only and has no end-user interface strings to localise.
know_common_errors_justification: The error classes specific to this software are documented and defended: credential exfiltration through untrusted workflow input (zizmor and the capability-boundary lint), unpinned actions and supply-chain substitution (every `uses:` pinned to a full commit SHA, every tool checksummed), and unsafe input handling in the fixture crates (a libFuzzer target with a committed corpus). The README's table of what proving here has caught is the running record. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
know_secure_design_justification: The security architecture this repository runs under is designed and documented in the governance repository: least privilege on every workflow permission block, an explicit capability boundary forbidding `id-token: write` in any workflow that runs caller-supplied code, keyless trusted publishing instead of long-lived tokens, and SLSA Build/Source/Dependency levels claimed only where evidence exists. This repository is where those controls are exercised first. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
license_location_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and the full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt, the REUSE-standard location. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/LICENSE
license_per_file_justification: Every file carries an SPDX licence statement (0BSD) through REUSE.toml, with the full text in LICENSES/0BSD.txt. `reuse lint` reports 180 of 180 files with licence information. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/REUSE.toml
maintained_justification: Actively maintained at rehearsal cadence — this repository releases more often than anything it proves for, because that is its function. Renovate and Dependabot keep every pin current, the Monday audit re-checks settings drift and link liveness, and the Thursday cold rebuild re-verifies the latest published release.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Actively maintained: releases are cut from conventional commits at rehearsal cadence, Renovate and Dependabot keep every pin current, and the scheduled audits re-check settings drift, link liveness and the reproducibility of the latest release. Only the newest release is supported, per the organisation's security policy. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
name: release-lab
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is committed. GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, trivy's secret rules run in the gate, and the design avoids long-lived credentials entirely: publishing is keyless via trusted publishing and OIDC.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Not measured, so not claimed. In practice fixes here arrive with the check that would have caught them — the artefact-class smoke tests and the fuzz corpus grew that way — but there is no measurement of the proportion and asserting 50% without one would be a guess.
release_notes_justification: Every release carries generated release notes: CHANGELOG.md is produced by git-cliff from conventional commits and the same summary is attached to the GitHub release. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a publicly known run-time vulnerability in this software. Advisories against dependencies are handled visibly rather than silently: the release path refuses to publish with an undecided advisory in its SBOM — it blocked v0.19.1 for RUSTSEC-2021-0127 — and each release ships the resulting VEX decisions as an asset (release-lab-0.24.4.vex.openvex.json). https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/releases
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands as a pull request with its own commits; the repository contains the full development history, not only released states.
repo_track_justification: Git records author, committer, timestamp and diff for every change; the history is protected by organisation rulesets and every revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation emitted by this repository's own reserved identity (source-attest.yml), so the record is independently verifiable rather than merely present.
report_archive_justification: The issue tracker is public, permanently archived and searchable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_process_justification: Bug reports are submitted through GitHub Issues using the organisation's issue forms; SUPPORT.md states where to ask. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: The tracker is small and nothing on it is unanswered: three issues in total, two closed with the resolution recorded in the closing pull request, and one open — Renovate's dependency dashboard, which is a standing status page rather than a report awaiting a reply. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues, used for every individual issue. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/issues
require_2FA_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide — GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation — so it covers pushing to the repository and access to private vulnerability reports alike.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and what each is responsible for. Who holds the maintainer role is unambiguous: the @monumental-archive/owners team, which CODEOWNERS routes every review to in every repository, and joining that team is what becoming a maintainer concretely means. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
secure_2FA_justification: The 2FA in use is cryptographic rather than SMS-based: GitHub's supported second factors here are TOTP and WebAuthn, and the organisation's requirement is satisfied without SMS.
security_review_justification: The governance repository's docs/build-assessment.md and docs/source-assessment.md are security reviews of exactly the machinery this repository runs, control by control, and they are current rather than historical — the scheduled audit re-checks them. This repository is the place those controls are exercised before any production repository. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/build-assessment.md
signed_releases_justification: Verified against the published release rather than asserted: v0.24.4 carries nine Sigstore evidence bundles (attestations-binaries, -image, -npm, -extensions and one per Postgres major) alongside checksums.txt, an SPDX SBOM and an OpenVEX document. Signing is keyless — Sigstore/Fulcio with a Rekor transparency-log entry — and is performed by the organisation's separate signer identity, which never sees the bytes. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/releases/tag/v0.24.4
sites_https_justification: The repository, its releases and its documentation are served by GitHub over HTTPS; there is no separate project website.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub; the project stores no passwords of its own.
small_tasks_justification: The organisation's labels exist ('good first issue', 'help wanted') but no issue in this repository currently carries either, so small tasks are not identified for a newcomer.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL is enforced organisation-wide for the languages in this repository, cargo-deny and osv-scanner match the dependency graph against advisory databases, and zizmor is a scanner specific to the other artefact here — GitHub Actions workflows — covering template injection, excessive permissions, credential persistence and unpinned actions.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed before merge — the gate blocks the pull request, and the organisation's static-analysis policy sets the remediation threshold at zero. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL default setup is enforced organisation-wide, and the gate runs cargo-deny and osv-scanner over the lockfile, shellcheck over shell, actionlint and zizmor over every workflow, and trivy over configuration — on every pull request, before any release.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every commit: the gate runs on every pull request and every push to main, with a scheduled Monday audit re-running the network-dependent checks and a Thursday cold rebuild of the latest published release.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Branch coverage is not measured: cargo-llvm-cov reports region coverage (86.57%) rather than branch coverage on the pinned stable toolchain, and a region is not a branch. Claiming the criterion from a proxy would be a guess dressed as a number.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: gate.yml runs the full gate on every push and pull request to main, calling the organisation's shared reusable workflow across a repository boundary. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/.github/workflows/gate.yml
test_invocation_justification: `mise run ci` — one command, identical locally and in CI. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/README.md
test_justification: `mise run ci` is the automated suite and it is what CI runs: it collects the organisation's lint belt, runs `cargo test --workspace --locked`, and enforces the committed coverage floor with cargo-llvm-cov. Identical locally and in the cloud, from the same lockfile. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/mise.toml
test_most_justification: The suite covers most of the code it measures: 87.10% line coverage over the crates tested on the gate runner, enforced by the coverage ratchet in `mise run ci`. Beyond unit tests, every version exercises the whole repository end to end — four artefact classes across five Postgres majors, each with a smoke test — because that release path is what this repository exists to prove.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' is the written policy: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it, and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' item 3, is the formal written policy: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Measured by the gate on every change, not asserted: `mise run ci` runs cargo-llvm-cov and the latest run reports 87.10% line and 86.57% region coverage, against a committed .coverage-floor of 69 that the ratchet only lets rise. Stated precisely, because the measurement has a boundary: it covers the crates whose tests run on the gate runner (lab-core, lab-wasm); lab-pg is excluded by COVERAGE_EXCLUDE because its pgrx tests need a live Postgres and run instead inside the extension class's own per-major containers during the release, and the lab-cli binary has no unit tests of its own — it is exercised end to end by the release path's binary smoke test. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/blob/main/.coverage-floor
test_statement_coverage90_justification: Statement coverage is measured (cargo-llvm-cov, ratcheted against the committed floor) and stands at 87.10% lines over the crates tested on the gate runner — short of 90, and honestly so.
tests_are_added_justification: New fixture behaviour arrives with its test: the parse-marker fuzz target and its committed corpus landed with the code they exercise, and each new artifact class landed with the smoke test the release path runs against it (scripts/image-smoke.sh, scripts/binary-smoke.sh).
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy is stated in the contributor-facing documentation itself: CONTRIBUTING.md, item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions'. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: With a single maintainer, no proposed modification is reviewed by a person other than its author. This is the Source L4 and Gold boundary for this project and is recorded as headcount-blocked in docs/slsa-reference.md; it is watched as an issue rather than papered over. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Every reused component is identified by exact version — Cargo.lock for crates, mise.lock for tools, full commit SHAs for actions — and updating is a Renovate pull request the gate verifies.
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning, derived from conventional commits by git-cliff.
version_tags_justification: Each release is identified by an immutable git tag (v*). https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/tags
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated tag objects signed with Sigstore keyless signing, and the signature travels in the tag object itself: v0.24.4 carries a PKCS#7 SIGNED MESSAGE whose Fulcio certificate binds it to the organisation's release workflow identity. GitHub reports such tags as unverified with reason no_user because the signer is a workflow identity rather than a GitHub account; the signature is present and checkable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/release-lab/tags
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique semantic version, tagged v<major>.<minor>.<patch> by the organisation's tag-minting GitHub App; tags are immutable under the organisation tag ruleset.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Critical vulnerabilities are fixed as they are identified; dependency updates are automated and the release gate blocks on the dependency checks.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity. cargo-deny and osv-scanner run in the gate, dependency-review runs on every pull request, Renovate and Dependabot open updates continuously, and the release path refuses to publish with an undecided advisory in the SBOM — RUSTSEC-2021-0127 was decided and published as a VEX statement rather than left unanswered.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit. SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters who do not request anonymity.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, so reports stay private until an advisory is published. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md publishes the process: private reporting through the repository's Security tab. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months, so there is no response time to report. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgement within 14 days.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process end to end: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, what to expect afterwards, and the scope. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: The tree builds and tests warning-free; the gate is red on any belt warning and no change merges red.
warnings_justification: rustc's warning set is on for every build and `cargo test --workspace --locked` surfaces it, and the shared lint belt runs shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor, typos, taplo and rumdl over every tracked file, where a warning is a failure — the gate exits non-zero and a red gate cannot merge.
warnings_strict_justification: Not maximally strict for Rust specifically: the shared belt has no clippy or `-D warnings` task, so rustc warnings are surfaced by the test run rather than turned into failures. Every other language in the tree is maximally strict (shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor, taplo, rumdl, typos, all failing the gate).
